Convert emmeans results to forest data

Source: R/as_forest_data_emmeans.R
as_forest_data_emmeans.Rd

Standardizes estimated marginal means and contrasts from emmeans into forest_data. emmeans::emmeans(), pairs(), and emmeans::contrast() all return emmGrid objects, so one method covers means, pairwise comparisons, and custom contrasts. Summaries from summary() and confint() (summary_emm) and emm_list results, such as emmeans(fit, pairwise ~ treatment), are supported too.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'emmGrid'
as_forest_data(
  data,
  ...,
  label = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  subgroup = NULL,
  term_labels = NULL,
  exponentiate = NULL,
  estimate_scale = NULL,
  effect_label = NULL,
  reference_value = NULL,
  conf.level = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  adjust = NULL,
  sort_terms = c("none", "descending", "ascending"),
  p_method = c("level", "overall")
)

# S3 method for class 'summary_emm'
as_forest_data(
  data,
  ...,
  label = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  subgroup = NULL,
  term_labels = NULL,
  exponentiate = NULL,
  estimate_scale = NULL,
  effect_label = NULL,
  reference_value = NULL,
  conf.level = NULL,
  sort_terms = c("none", "descending", "ascending"),
  p_method = c("level", "overall")
)

# S3 method for class 'emm_list'
as_forest_data(data, ..., which = 1L)

Arguments

data

An emmGrid, summary_emm, or emm_list object from emmeans.

...

Not used; must be empty.

label

Optional column used as the displayed row label instead of the composed label.

group

Optional column used to color and dodge estimates that share a row, such as a by variable.

facet

Optional column used to split rows into plot sections.

subgroup

Optional column used to group rows under hierarchical headers, such as "term" for several contrasts of one factor. Rows are gathered into contiguous blocks in order of first appearance.

term_labels

Optional named vector used to relabel identifier values (for example c(hp = "Horsepower")) or composed row labels.

exponentiate

NULL keeps the reported scale. TRUE converts log-scale estimates to ratios and FALSE converts ratios to the log scale.

estimate_scale

Optional override for the detected effect scale. One of "identity", "log", "ratio", "probability", or "risk_difference".

effect_label

Optional override for the effect label used on the axis and in tables.

reference_value

Optional override for the reference line value. Use NULL for no reference line.

conf.level

For emmGrid objects, the confidence level passed to summary(). NULL uses the emmeans default. For summary_emm objects, NULL uses the stored level and a number must match it.

type

Optional prediction type passed to summary(), such as "response" to back-transform means or obtain ratio contrasts.

adjust

Optional multiplicity adjustment passed to summary().

sort_terms

How to sort rows: "none", "descending", or "ascending".

p_method

Subgroup p-value placement when subgroup is mapped. Defaults to "level" because emmeans reports one test per row.

which

For emm_list objects, the element to convert, by position or name. Defaults to the first element, matching emmeans methods.

Value

A forest_data object. The original grid and by columns are retained for table helpers.

Details

emmGrid objects are summarized with confidence intervals at conf.level and with adjust and type passed to summary(). Contrasts also include their tests; means do not, because a test against zero is rarely meaningful. summary_emm objects are used exactly as computed, so conf.level can only confirm the stored level.

Row labels come from the primary variables, such as the factor levels or the contrast column. When by variables vary they are added to the label unless they are mapped to group, facet, or subgroup, for example facet = "sex".

The effect scale follows the estimate column chosen by emmeans:

  • Contrasts (estimate) are additive with a reference line at 0. On a log or logit link they are log ratios or log odds ratios, and exponentiate = TRUE converts them to ratios.

  • Back-transformed contrasts (ratio and odds.ratio) are ratios on a log10 axis with a reference line at 1.

  • Marginal means (emmean, response, rate, and similar) have no null value, so no reference line is drawn. Probabilities (prob) use the probability scale.

Intervals and p-values reflect any multiplicity adjustment applied by emmeans, such as the Tukey adjustment used by pairs().

See also

as_forest_data(), ggforestplot()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("emmeans", quietly = TRUE)) {
  warp <- lm(breaks ~ wool * tension, data = warpbreaks)

  # Marginal means for each tension level, faceted by wool
  means <- emmeans::emmeans(warp, ~ tension | wool)
  ggforestplot(means, facet = "wool")

  # Tukey-adjusted pairwise differences
  ggforestplot(pairs(means), facet = "wool")

  # Odds ratios from a logistic model
  fit <- glm(vs ~ factor(gear) + mpg, data = mtcars, family = binomial())
  gear_pairs <- pairs(emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ gear), adjust = "none")
  as_forest_data(gear_pairs, exponentiate = TRUE)
}

#> 3 gear4 - gear5 495.0415935 1.2614350 1.942757e+05 gear4 - gear5 estimate  <NA>
#>   subgroup grouping separate_groups    n events    p.value      contrast
